captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a half-oloid, a geometric shape derived from cutting a full oloid along its plane of symmetry. The curved, convex outer surface transitions smoothly between two perpendicular circular arcs, creating a highly organic and aerodynamic appearance. The flat, cut face is square-like with curved edges, featuring two cylindrical alignment pegs on one axis and two matching cylindrical socket holes on the perpendicular axis. These features allow two identical half-oloid pieces to be printed flat on a 3D printer bed and securely joined together to form a complete, seamless oloid.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric oloid in OpenSCAD with options to render either a full oloid or a half-oloid split along its flat symmetry plane. The half-oloid option should include customizable alignment pegs and corresponding holes on the flat mating surface to facilitate easy 3D printing and assembly, controlled by parameters for radius, peg height, and peg gap tolerance.
captions.factory: The code defines a core 'oloid' module by applying the hull() operator to two perpendicular, thin cylinders (using cylinder with h=0.1) offset by their radius. The 'halfOloid' module creates the split version by using difference() to cut the full oloid with a large cube, then subtracts two peg holes along one axis. It then uses union() to add two cylindrical pegs along the perpendicular axis of the flat cut surface, rotating the cylinders and positioning them with a for-loop. A top-level conditional block selects between the full 'oloid' and 'halfOloid' modules based on the '_type' parameter.
